gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost of each candidate per rated Wh, or the Tenergy T320's maker-stated true 320 Wh delivered through two 12 V 8 A DC5521 sockets with no inverter in the path. On a 20 W router-and-modem load that comes to about 16 h for $225.99 ($0.75/Wh). The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 gets about 11.8 h for $289.99 ($1.01/Wh) once BLUETTI's own 4.5 W standby draw is added to the load.
standout_why: I compared against homepowerfacts.com (cited), outagemath.com (cited), backupcalc.com (cited) and runtimemath.com. None gives any price-based figure: no cost per Wh and no cost per backup hour. homepowerfacts lists list prices only for other models, and has no price for the RIVER 3. runtimemath lists a 9 W draw for the Elite 30 V2, which conflicts with BLUETTI's own 4.5 W claim. No page names a candidate's DC5521 12 V port or gives an hours-on-DC figure for a named model. backupcalc only applies a generic 90% DC efficiency. None covers the Tenergy T320 at all, or its 320 Wh actual capacity.
decides: This confirms a split pick instead of overturning one. For hours per dollar on a 12 V router and modem, the Tenergy T320 wins: $0.75 per rated Wh, two 12 V 8 A barrel sockets, and up to about 16 h at 20 W. But Tenergy publishes no UPS or switchover claim. If the network must stay up without a reboot, the Elite 30 V2 is still the pick, because it has the only maker-stated ≤10 ms UPS among the prices I could read, at about $25 per backup hour versus about $14 for the T320.
